bugs: Minor: the fallback price_cents is not cast to int in ShippingQuoteController.php:22. It only becomes a string if someone sets config at runtime as a string (a probe returned "1295"). The config file already casts it, so production is unaffected.
antipatterns: app/Services/CarrierClient.php:31 sets only timeout(1.5) and no connectTimeout. The total timeout still caps each attempt, so this is acceptable, but the connect budget is implicit.
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:41 checks only that rates is an array, not the shape of each item. A probe showed a malformed item passes straight through to checkout.
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:9 declares a global const in the test file, which leaks into the global namespace.
strengths: Http::retry(3, 0, when) uses a transient-only predicate (ConnectionException or serverError), so 404 and 401 are never retried. Probes confirmed a single call for 429/400/401/404.
Worst case is 3 × 1.5s = 4.5s with zero sleep, which stays inside the 5s budget. A comment documents that invariant.
Exception mapping is clean: domain exceptions plus a `never`-typed handleFailure. Only the 401 calls report(), so flaky 5xx responses don't create alert noise.
Uses a FormRequest with validated('postcode'), and the controller is thin.

Http::preventStrayRequests is applied globally in Pest.php. Tests use Exceptions::fake/assertReported and cover the 401-not-retried case, no reports for transient failures, a malformed body, a configured fallback, timeouts and recovery after a 5xx.

bugs: app/Services/CarrierClient.php:74-77: a 200 response with a rate item missing service or price_cents crashes with ErrorException 'Undefined array key' and returns HTTP 500 to checkout instead of the fallback (confirmed by probe). The defensive normalisation it adds is itself the crash site.

ShippingQuoteController.php:25 reports every CarrierUnavailableException, including ordinary transient 5xx and timeouts. Reporting the 401 alone, which is the alerting signal the task asks for, gets drowned in flaky-carrier noise.
antipatterns: app/Services/CarrierClient.php:30-61 hand-rolls a for/continue retry loop with a $last variable instead of using Http::retry() with a when-callback.
ShippingQuoteController.php:15-17 validates inline with $request->validate(...)['postcode'] rather than through a FormRequest.
ShippingQuoteController.php:19-33 uses mutable $estimated/$rates assignments across the try/catch branches, which is harder to follow than returning early.
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:74 uses array_values(array_map(...)) where collect()->map()->values() would be the idiomatic choice.
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:101-105 hooks into reportable()->stop() on the handler instead of using Exceptions::fake().
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:13 has a misleading comment ('1s connect + 1.5s total'). Guzzle's timeout already includes the connect time.
strengths: Sets both connectTimeout(1) and timeout(1.5) with no sleeps, giving a 4.5s worst case.
Retries only connection errors and 5xx. 401, 404 and other 4xx fail fast, and probes confirmed single calls.
Http::preventStrayRequests is used, and tests cover the 401 no-retry case, malformed bodies, retry-then-success and a configured fallback.

bugs: The test suite really sleeps: retry(3, 100) runs without Sleep::fake(), so the suite takes about 1.5s versus about 0.2s for the others. Pest.php imports Sleep and Http but never uses them.
There is no Http::preventStrayRequests. Tests such as 'requires a postcode' run without a fake, so a regression could hit the real network.
antipatterns: tests/Pest.php:4-5 has unused imports for Http and Sleep, apparently a fake-sleep/stray-request setup that was planned but never wired in.
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:61-63 is a reflection test (is_subclass_of ShouldntReport) rather than a behavioural one.
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:126-131 and 146-151 register reportable() closures that return false instead of using Exceptions::fake().
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:7-8 shares fixtures through file-scope $rates/$fallback variables captured by `use`, which is awkward in Pest.
routes/api.php:11 adds a throttle:60,1 middleware nobody asked for.

app/Services/CarrierClient.php:27 puts an inline comment inside the fluent chain. app/Services/CarrierClient.php:41 also reports every other 4xx and malformed payloads, which is broader than asked but defensible.
strengths: Uses Http::retry with a when-callback and a 100ms sleep, and retries 429 sensibly. The budget is 3 × 1.4s + 0.2s = 4.4s, and it also sets connectTimeout(1).
UnknownPostcode implements ShouldntReport and render(), so the controller only handles the fallback. The digits:4 rule is idiomatic.
Reports only the 401 and other non-transient failures, never 5xx or 429.

Tests use Http::failedConnection/pushFailedConnection, which are the modern fake helpers, and cover the 401 no-retry case, no reports for transient failures, malformed payloads and the configured fallback.

v.rationale:
I ran the test suite for all three; every one passes. I also put nine throwaway probes through each one (429, 400, a malformed rate item, an HTML 200, a connection error then 404, 500 then 401, a string fallback config, newline and fullwidth-digit postcodes, and the timeout options), then deleted them.

impl-1 is the cleanest. It uses Http::retry with a transient-only predicate and zero sleep inside a documented 4.5s budget. It maps the domain exceptions with a never-typed helper and reports only the 401. It uses a FormRequest, a global preventStrayRequests and Exceptions::fake in tests. I found no real bugs.

impl-3 is close behind on production code: ShouldntReport/render on the exception, digits:4, and a sensible 429 retry. It loses ground on test hygiene: real sleeps because Sleep is never faked, no preventStrayRequests, unused imports in Pest.php, a reflection-only test and hand-rolled reportable hooks. It also adds an unrequested throttle middleware.

impl-2 hand-rolls the retry loop, validates inline and reports every transient failure, which buries the 401 alert in noise. It also has a real bug I confirmed with a probe: a 200 response with a malformed rate item crashes with an undefined-key ErrorException and returns 500 to checkout instead of the fallback.
